lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato | Lesson 33 -- Pause and Rewind
lesson.grammar_point: must and mustn't for rules and strong advice, and mustn't vs don't have to (you must stay near the peak, you mustn't drop in, you don't have to catch ten waves)

listenings.text: Hi Renato, it's Dana. Thanks for today. That was a really useful session. Here are the three rules we wrote, so you don't forget them. Rule one: you must stay in position near the peak. Don't drift to the shoulder. Rule two: you mustn't waste waves. A small wave in the first minute is a mistake. Patience wins heats. Rule three: you don't have to catch ten waves. Two good waves are enough. Oh, and one more thing. You mustn't paddle behind a surfer with priority. That's interference, and the penalty is really big. Okay. Watch the replay again on Saturday, but only once. You don't have to watch it every night!

Hey mate, it's Kai. I've just read the rules for the semifinal on the website, and there are some new things. First, every surfer must wear a colored jersey, but you don't have to bring one. They give it to you on the beach. Second, you must check in at seven, at the tent near the parking lot. If you're late, you can't surf. And the heats are twenty-five minutes now, not twenty. One more thing: phones. You mustn't use your phone in the competitors' area. Leave it with Bev. That's it. See you at training tomorrow!

items.situation: Jess asks: "Do I have to bring my own jersey to the semifinal?" The organizers give the jerseys on the beach. Answer her.
A grommet wants to paddle behind a surfer with priority. Stop him and explain the rule.
Tom asks what time you must be at the beach on Saturday. Check-in is at seven. Tell him.
Bev says: "Watch the replay again tonight!" You watched it twice today. Answer her nicely.
Your teacher asks about rules in your real life: at school, at home or in a sport you like. Say one thing you must do and one thing you mustn't do.
